title: kbcommon.url_holds_credential reads a Windows path with an @ in a folder name as a credential url
goal: kbroot.py add-remote and check.py accept a Windows path url such as C:\work\jan@corp.example.com\team.git (no credential), and keep refusing a user:password@ and an http(s) token@ url; a token in a url's query or fragment is considered (SP-c6w5hjmc review gap 7)

run:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import kbcommon
bad = kbcommon.url_holds_credential("C:\\work\\jan@corp.example.com\\team.git")
print("a Windows path with an @ in a folder name is read as a credential url:", bad)
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
